newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends firmer on FOMC decision.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends firmer on FOMC decision.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed slightly firmer on Tuesday after the Federal Open Market Committee announced it would not change U.S. interest rate policy in the final minutes of trade, dealers said.
"The FOMC decision cleared the way for the peso to keep on gaining ground in the coming days," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate both ended 0.2 of a centavo firmer at 7.8760/7.8800 and 7.8730/7.8780 per dollar, respectively.
The FOMC announced it had decided to leave the federal funds rate unchanged at 5.50 percent and the discount rate at 5.0 percent.
Dealers said peso strength could be curbed, however, as dollar puts previously auctioned by the central bank had been exercised on Monday and Tuesday.
"I feel we have strong resistance for the peso at 7.8600 per dollar," another trader said.
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed 0.4 of a centavo firmer at 7.8800/7.8830 per dollar.
Dealers estimated a trading range of 7.8650/7.8850 per dollar for the 48-hour peso on Wednesday.
